question: Does the broad southern MACS1931 Lenstool halo posterior overlap a wider-field concentration of plausible cluster galaxies that the existing 300 kpc member catalog misses?

coordinate_and_matching.frame: east-positive x and north-positive y; Lenstool posterior x is sign-flipped

selection_variants.rule: extended, clean r/i/z SNR>=5, z_phot_l68_i<=0.352<=z_phot_u68_i, and 0.20<=z_phot_median_i<=0.50
extended, clean r/i/z SNR>=5, z_phot_l95_i<=0.352<=z_phot_u95_i, and 0.10<=z_phot_median_i<=0.60
extended, clean r/i/z SNR>=5; contamination control only

density_test.statistic: posterior-mean Gaussian galaxy density evaluated at all retained second-halo centers
density_test.null: rotate every posterior halo center by the same nonzero angle around the fixed cluster center; galaxy positions, radii, weights, and survey footprint remain fixed

limits: Legacy Surveys photo-z values are not spectroscopy and the sightline is crowded with foreground stars.
The same lens observations generated the target halo posterior; an overdensity match would identify a plausible baryonic counterpart, not validate gravity routing.
The target halo position is broad and model-dependent.
The acquisition field is rectangular; the rotation null is interpreted only because all rotated posterior centers remain inside the frozen field.
This is a spent-system diagnostic and cannot promote a universal formula.
